A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPDMark by the same authors. All 18 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark extraction, video quality, attack robustness, temporal forensics, and ablation results on SVD-XT and ModelScope, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for extended training, frame regeneration, model modifications, and detection-threshold sensitivity in Section 4.5.1 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes per-frame message generation: v1 hashes the concatenation of watermark key kappa and frame index using Kbase; v2 hashes the frame index using a video-level Kbase. Verification correspondingly requires Kbase rather than kappa. The decoder basis selection, LoRA components, extractor, losses, and matching procedure otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: OpenVid-1M training, VBench prompts, and the image-to-video and text-to-video tasks remain. Appendix D substantially extends tested conditions through diffusion/VAE frame regeneration, adversarial decoder retraining, and false-alarm evaluation on non-watermarked videos. These broaden input and threat scenarios beyond the retained output-video perturbations; no new dataset is identified.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain VideoShield, VideoSeal, and VidSig as comparators on both main models. Newly discussed compression methods are attack mechanisms, and additional generative models are transfer settings, not added watermarking baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D revises several stated attack settings: blur changes from a 7x7 kernel with sigma 1.5 to 11x11 with sigma 2.0; random rotations become fixed 15-degree rotations; insertion changes from 20% of frames to one frame; trimming changes from 20% at each end to two frames. Denoising changes from bilateral filtering to Gaussian smoothing. New protocols include regeneration fractions, model transfer, INT8 quantization, threshold sweeps, and an additional 6k/12k training steps for G2/G3. These reported revisions do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.5.1 adds continued-training experiments to distinguish capacity effects from insufficient optimization. Appendix D.2-D.4 adds frame-regeneration robustness, denoiser transfer, quantization, decoder fine-tuning, and detection-threshold sensitivity analyses. Existing sampling and temporal-forensics analyses are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version provides explicit repeated-run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, or variability estimates. The binomial hypothesis-testing procedure in Equations 14-15 is retained. The new threshold heatmaps report detection rates at additional operating points, not a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes SPDMark's ModelScope SC/BC/MS/IQ from 0.900/0.937/0.960/0.555 to 0.948/0.968/0.972/0.623, reversing its quality ranking against the unchanged baselines; bit accuracy remains 0.988. Table 2 replaces ModelScope attack scores and changes its reported average from 0.944 to 0.939, but revised attack settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting loss. Figure 3 and the ModelScope sampling table, Table 5 in v1 and Table 6 in v2, also change. New results include extended-training recovery, regeneration and transfer performance, threshold-dependent detection, and extraction failure near 0.65 bit accuracy after decoder fine-tuning.

T1.justification: Equation 9 substantively revises the formal message definition from Trunc_M(H(Kbase,[kappa,t])) to Trunc_M(H(Kbase,t)). The displacement equations, loss definitions, binomial assumptions, verification derivation, and quality-metric formulas otherwise remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: key-conditioned parameter displacement, efficient multi-key embedding without per-key retraining, frame-specific watermarking, and alignment-based temporal forensics. Additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets high-payload degradation as partly an optimization-budget effect, supported by continued training, rather than presenting only the capacity trade-off. Appendix D adds a substantive applicability boundary: robustness to denoiser changes and quantization does not extend to adversarial decoder retraining because the decoder must remain consistent with the learned dictionary. It also explains regeneration recovery and threshold trade-offs. Section 4.4 replaces the earlier quality-degradation discussion with interpretations of the revised ModelScope results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access hyperlink and newly discloses a 2k-step recovery-only training phase before combined losses; this does not establish a changed training schedule. It documents identical compute for Figure 3, STTN preprocessing, and simulated per-channel INT8 quantization. Conversely, some attack details become less explicit, including subtitle parameters, vignetting strength, and the adjacent-swap proportion. Most optimizer, hardware, training-budget, and cost information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the post-hoc watermarking citation to Saha's Hidden Trigger Backdoor Attacks with Zhu's HiDDeN. It adds references for Balle and Cheng compression, STTN inpainting, and Zhao's generative watermark-removal work. Some categorical descriptions of prior-method limitations are softened, while the overall research positioning remains stable. Publication and bibliographic updates to retained works are not new citations.

P1.justification: Most introductory and methodological prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 edits terminology, condenses repetitive results discussion, revises captions, adds author contact information and a contents page, and subdivides Appendix D. The added scientific analyses do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column design with a two-column layout, resizing and repositioning figures, tables, and equations throughout. Figure 3 is redrawn with revised axis and legend presentation; a regeneration table and three-panel threshold heatmap are added. Existing qualitative examples are retained, with appendix Figures 4-5 becoming Figures 5-6, rather than replaced by new examples.

improvement.justification: The extended-training control and Appendix D analyses make important robustness claims more assessable and reveal a decoder-retraining failure absent from v1. The disclosed training schedule and code link also improve documentation. These gains are tempered by reduced specificity in some attack recipes and unexplained revisions to protocols and ModelScope scores, which limit comparative interpretation. The evidence supports a net improvement, but not a substantial overall advance based merely on additional experiments or higher reported quality scores.
